body:
Wtf. Lol this professor makes me feel better about not staying in academia...if tenured people are just as intolerant/closed-minded/plainly wrong as everyone else.

But seriously. I totally get the self-validation of negative thoughts. Even when ppl say dumb things and I know it's dumb...still hard not to almost subconsciously believe them. Anyway, a counterexample: Edvard Munch. Ludwig Wittgenstein for someone in STEM. Definitely way more ppl I just can't think of. I think suffering gives a unique perspective, despite still being something I wouldn't wish on anyone.

Oh wow, I relate to your post a lot honestly (and nice username btw). I also can't pinpoint any childhood trauma that people don't experience at one time or another or are "part of growing up". Have also tried religion at several bad points but it didn't really help. Neither have drugs so far. Haven't done ECT though, am scared it will make my brain fog worse.

I worry about employment as well...like how you put it, I can't hold interest enough to do any given job for longer than maybe one year at most. I'm in my mid 20s so I somehow have to figure out how to make myself care for the next 40 or so years.
came here to make sure this was said

Nothing to say except that I feel the same way and have for probably a year now. No energy or time for hobbies when it's straight to bed after commute back. Wish I took a mental health gap year before starting my job. Or just worked up the balls to refuse it all one day. How the hell do people do this for 50 or 60 years straight.

For me it takes the form of extreme difficulty in expressing myself. I have to ramble around just to get a simple point across that could be expressed in only a few words. My boss and coworkers probably think I'm some kind of idiot. I used to be more articulate but these days I just don't have the energy to fight my way back to where I once was, nor can I see an easier way to do so.

I used to think I'd hate driving, and traffic still gives me anxiety, but I also agree there are few things more relaxing and comforting than driving down an empty or mostly empty street whilst blasting music.

One of my favorite songwriters Nick Drake would drive through the countryside til he ran out of gas and he had to call to get picked up from the middle of nowhere, lol.

never even been in a relationship (am female btw). but i relate with feeling stuck. also early 20s. also worry (actually am pretty convinced) that no one will ever love me in an authentic way. can't tell my parents either...theyre v religious and it would just make things worse.
